guidelines.detail: refines COL-03 (The description connects the chef's work to the employee's handoff, while the validator identifies the chef's start event as detached. COL-03 establishes which flow type to use within or between participants; this guideline adds that the receiving work must be connected to the handoff.)

documentation rule COL-03 not applied (The description assigns the handoff and subsequent work to roles within the restaurant process. The validator records show a message flow between elements in the same pool, so the issue is the choice of flow type, not a missing element. COL-03 already states to use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants.)

documentation rule EVT-03 not applied (The description says the guest waits until it is his turn (S2). The reference models that wait as an intermediate catch event (M5), while the generated model uses a task instead (X2), with the corresponding flows also differing (F2, F7). EVT-03 already gives this guidance.)

same as LRN-037 (The description specifies distinct events and activities, while the label pairs show differences in how those semantics are expressed. The proposed guidance is already captured by learned guideline LRN-037, which calls for labels to preserve distinctions between elements.)

documentation rule COL-01 not applied (The description distinguishes the guest, employee, and chef and describes communications among them. The records show a participant omitted, a reversed message flow, and several missing message flows. COL-01 already requires a pool for each distinct interacting participant, while COL-04 and FID-01 cover directing message flows and modeling described messages, so this guideline is already covered.)

same as LRN-039 (The description says the employee informs the chef before the chef prepares the meal, while the validator identifies a detached start-to-end chain. LRN-039 already gives essentially the same guidance for work following a handoff.)

documentation rule COL-03 not applied (The description has the employee inform the chef, whose work follows, while the validator reports a message flow connecting elements in the same pool. COL-03 already says to use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between participants.)

refines FID-01 (The description states that the employee prepares and passes the buzzer to the guest. The missing flows show that the preparation and handover activities were not represented, while the generated buzzer event is not a substitute for those actions. This makes the guideline a specific application of FID-01’s instruction to model every distinct activity and event stated in the description.)

The reference directs the message flow from collecting money to paying money, but the description places payment before the employee’s subsequent actions. Since the reference direction conflicts with the described order, it cannot support a guideline to reproduce that collaboration model.

same as LRN-039 (The validator identifies a detached start-to-end chain, while the description says the chef’s work follows the employee’s notification. The learned guideline LRN-039 already covers connecting receiving work to that handoff.)

documentation rule COL-03 not applied (The description places the employee-to-chef handoff within the restaurant, while the generated message flow connects elements in the same pool. COL-03 already says to use sequence flows within one participant and message flows between participants.)

documentation rule EVT-03 not applied (The description says the guest waits for their turn, while the generated model represents that wait as a task and the reference as an intermediate catch event. EVT-03 already gives the same modeling guidance for flow waiting for a trigger, so this is not a new rule.)

same as LRN-037 (The description distinguishes learning that a meal is ready from the later handover, while the generated event label conflates them (P2, S8, S10, S12). This applies the learned guideline to preserve distinctions between events and activities.)

refines COL-01 (The missing participant and message-flow records, alongside the described handoffs and notifications, support this guideline. It refines COL-01 by specifying how to represent the described exchanges; COL-04 addresses message-flow direction. C2 is not cited because the reference direction appears inconsistent with the described guest-to-employee payment.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents one participant's work as following a handoff from another participant: Model the receiving work as connected to that handoff: use sequence flow within the same process, or a message flow to a message-triggered start or catch event in a separate process, rather than an unconnected start-to-end chain.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents one participant's work as following a handoff from another participant

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description shows work being handed from one role to another within a single participant process

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that process flow pauses until a stated condition or event occurs

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes multiple activities or events by their action, information, or outcome: Label each corresponding BPMN element to preserve those distinctions, rather than using interchangeable or overly generic labels.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description distinguishes process elements by their action, trigger, or outcome

rules_sent_back.instruction: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies distinct actors who perform work and communicate with one another, including by transferring information or physical items.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description explicitly states that a participant prepares a physical item for transfer and gives it to another participant, while also describing a later event involving that item.: Model the preparation and transfer as activities; do not use the later event involving the item as a substitute for either activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly states that a participant prepares a physical item for transfer and gives it to another participant, while also describing a later event involving that item.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies distinct participants and describes information or items being communicated or handed off between them: Model each participant as a separate pool and represent each described exchange between participants with a message flow from sender to receiver, using valid interaction nodes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies distinct participants and describes information or items being communicated or handed off between them
